questions.question: There are 8 apples in a basket. 3 are red. What fraction of the apples are red?
questions.explain: Put the red apples (3) on top and ALL the apples (8) on the bottom. A common trap is putting the non-red count in the bottom instead of the total.

questions.question: A bag has 6 socks. 2 are blue. What fraction of the socks are blue?
questions.explain: The top is the blue socks (2) and the bottom is ALL the socks (6). The non-blue socks do not replace the total in the bottom.

questions.question: There are 10 pencils on a desk. 4 are yellow. What fraction of the pencils are yellow?
questions.explain: Yellow pencils (4) go on top and ALL pencils (10) go on the bottom. The not-yellow count (6) does not belong in the fraction.

questions.question: A box has 9 candies. 3 are green. What fraction of the candies are green?
questions.explain: Green candies (3) go on top, all candies (9) on the bottom. The bottom number is always the whole group, not the non-green ones.

questions.question: Lily puts 12 buttons on a shelf. 5 are brown. What fraction of the buttons are brown?
questions.explain: Brown buttons (5) on top, all buttons (12) on the bottom. Putting the non-brown count (7) in the bottom is a common slip.

questions.question: A class has 16 students. 9 wear sneakers. What fraction of the students wear sneakers?
questions.explain: Sneaker-wearers (9) go on top, all students (16) go on the bottom. The 7 who do not wear sneakers is not part of the fraction.

questions.question: A basket holds 14 eggs. 6 are white. What fraction of the eggs are white?
questions.explain: White eggs (6) on top, all eggs (14) on the bottom. The 8 non-white eggs are not the bottom number.

questions.question: A jar has 15 jellybeans. 6 are purple. 2 of the purple ones are chewed. What fraction of ALL the jellybeans are chewed purple ones?
questions.explain: The question asks about ALL 15 jellybeans, so 15 goes on the bottom and the 2 chewed purple ones go on top. A trap is using 6 (the purple ones) as the bottom.

questions.question: A bag has some apples. 4 are red. The fraction of red apples is 4/9. How many apples are in the bag?
questions.explain: The bottom number (9) tells you the total group. The top (4) is the red ones. A common trap is subtracting 4 from 9 to get 5, but the bottom is the whole, not the rest.

questions.question: Out of 12 toys, some are stuffed animals. The fraction of stuffed animals is 5/12. How many toys are stuffed animals?
questions.explain: The top number (5) tells you how many are stuffed animals. A trap is subtracting 5 from 12 to get 7, but that gives the NOT stuffed animals, not the stuffed ones.

questions.question: Zoe says: 'There are 8 crackers. 3 are salty. So the fraction of salty crackers is 3/5.' What did Zoe do wrong?
options: She added the salty and not-salty crackers.
She put all the crackers on the top number.
She put the 5 not-salty ones on the bottom.
She counted the salty crackers twice on top.
questions.explain: Zoe used 5 (the not-salty crackers) in the bottom instead of 8 (all crackers). The bottom number must always be the whole group.

questions.question: Noah packs 7 grapes in his lunch box. 2 of the grapes are green. What fraction of the grapes are green?
questions.explain: The whole group is 7 grapes, so 7 is the bottom number. The 2 green grapes go on top, which makes the one that says 2/7. Do not put 5 on the bottom; 5 is only the grapes that are not green.

questions.question: Mia borrows 11 books from the library. 4 of them are about animals. What fraction of the books are about animals?
questions.explain: Count the whole pile first: 11 books, so 11 goes on the bottom. The 4 animal books go on top, giving the one that says 4/11.

questions.question: Liam counts 9 rain boots by the classroom door. 5 of the boots are black. What fraction of the boots are black?
questions.explain: The bottom number is the whole group of 9 boots, and the top number is the 5 black ones, so it is the one that says 5/9. Writing 9 on top flips the fraction and makes it wrong.
